items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: I had been in the studio with people like Randy Weston, Mundell Lowe, Billy Taylor, you know all pussycats.

ctx.x: Well I must admit that I look back on it with a good deal of satisfaction. I’ve been very fortunate because in this business in particular, a lot of the associations that you form, at least initially, are accidental as hell. If someone tells me that I have been helpful to this or that career that’s exactly the thing that I want to hear because I have always looked on the role of the producer in a very specific way. Now one of the hardest things, and I’ve been at it, I’m getting perilously close to my fiftieth…

with doing this. The only real serious variation is that I have — I used to say in recent years — but for a lot of years, a lot of my attention has been focused on reissues and obviously the procedures are a little different there. For the most part that makes it possible to get into cliches like well I spent the whole day in the studio with Louis Armstrong or Duke Ellington or Fats Waller, and he didn’t give me a hard time. But that joke got busted about a year ago because one of my most recent reissue projects…

items.title: Billy Taylor — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: he and Bill Grower. So we struck up a relationship.

ctx.x: Actually I left Prestege and went with Riverside records. I was in… I was impressed by [Unintelligible] because I thought that they had a better merchandising… they had run a magazine and they seemed to have… they had gotten the stamp, the theolonious Monk stamp had come about. So I thought these guys know how to promote jazz. I mean they have got Time Magazine. Let me check on them. They were right around the corner from Prestege records, their office. So I went around and I had met Oron because I was interested…

had which talked about the traditional jazz and a lot of stuff, he and Bill Grower. So we struck up a relationship. I just made a decision. I think I will go over and try these guys for a while. So when I went over, he asked me what I wanted to do. And I said, “Well one of the things I would like to do is, I said I love the flute.” One of my favorite musicians is Frank Wess.
